propositions: Concurrent reducer cache writers can mutate the same temporary file inode after one writer renames it into place, causing the final cache to hold a current-generation hash with stale state fields from another generation.
The fixed `.cache.json.tmp` pathname is shared between `write_cache` in `_cache.py` and corrupt-CREATE handling in `_processors.py`, creating overlapping file descriptor races.
A cache hit on a corrupted envelope with mismatched generation hash and stale state bypasses deterministic replay, violating event-sourced invariants.
Serialized reducer execution produces no false cache hits, proving the defect is specific to concurrent divergent-generation writers.
The repair routes all cache publication through canonical `atomic_write` with unique temps, ensuring coherent envelope atomicity under concurrency.
